headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets while awesome-prompts is an unverified prompt source with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can be attacker-controlled instructions. nullclaw can ingest files, stdin/stdout, browser content, and MCP/tool outputs, so if the pair is bridged through shared files or copy-paste, prompt injection is plausible. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is copied into nullclaw prompts or files
IF nullclaw parses repository text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Review imported prompt files before use
Keep awesome-prompts content in a read-only folder
Disable automatic execution of file contents as instructions
Add provenance labels to imported prompts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and secrets, and has broad network egress; awesome-prompts is a prompt repository with no stated sensitive-data handling. If both share a workspace, nullclaw can expose local contents through logs, webhooks, or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is inferred, but nullclaw's surfaces make it credible.
conditions: IF both agents share ~/.nullclaw/workspace or another common directory
IF nullclaw sends workspace contents to external APIs or webhooks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Store secrets outside shared directories
Disable outbound sync for imported prompt files
Review audit-log retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; awesome-prompts is a repository of prompts that may also be edited or synced as files. If both operate on the same checkout or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite changes. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking guarantee.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace path
IF git operations occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate clone directories
Pause one agent during git writes
Use file locks around shared paths
Review for uncommitted changes before each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt text that nullclaw may treat as authoritative input, and nullclaw can then act through browsers, shell, MCP, or webhooks. That creates a plausible chain where unverified prompt content cascades into downstream actions. Because the pairwise handoff is not directly documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses imported prompt text as task instructions
IF downstream actions are triggered without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before action execution
Mark imported prompts as untrusted
Add a verification step before browser or shell actions
Log source provenance for each instruction
requires-engineering: implement policy gates for delegated actions

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, audit logs, and workspace files, while awesome-prompts is a public prompt repository with no residency or retention controls stated. If sensitive operational data is copied into the prompt repo or shared workspace, retention and disclosure policies can diverge. Only nullclaw is cited because the compliance risk is driven by its handling of regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal data are stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between the repository and nullclaw logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of prompt repositories
Review nullclaw log retention settings
Restrict access to ~/.nullclaw/workspace
Delete copied secrets after use
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
